content: Supabase (2026) recommends asymmetric JWT signing keys (ES256/RS256). Backend verifies tokens using the 'jose' library: createRemoteJWKSet(new URL('https://<ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/jwks')) then jwtVerify(token, jwks). Public keys are safe to publish; JWKS is edge-cached 10min. Legacy approach used a shared HS256 JWT secret verified with jsonwebtoken/jose. Verification extracts kid from JWT header, matches against JWKS. This is the mechanism behind a thin verifyUser(token) wrapper in Express.
